## Task
An anonymous black-box problem with 2 continuous inputs in [0, 1] and 2 competing objectives: `f1` (minimize), `f2` (minimize).

## Inputs
| parameter | type | domain | scale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x_fd1` | real | [0, 1] | linear |
| `x_dca` | real | [0, 1] | linear |

## Outputs
- `f1`: objective; minimize (lower is better).
- `f2`: objective; minimize (lower is better).

Goal: find a good set of trade-offs (an approximation of the Pareto front); quality is the hypervolume dominated by the feasible evaluated points relative to the reference point [18, 6] (order: f1, f2).

## Noise
Observations are noiseless: repeated evaluations of the same input return the same value.

Hypervolume dominated by a set of points relative to reference r: the set of points in objective space that are dominated by at least one point in the set and also dominate (or are between) the reference point.

Formally, for a point p to contribute to the hypervolume relative to reference r, we consider the box with corners p and r. If p dominates r (p_i ≤ r_i for all i), the box is [p1,r1]×[p2,r2] and its area is (r1-p1)×(r2-p2). If p does not dominate r (e.g., p1<r1 but p2>r2), then p contributes nothing on its own to the region beyond r — but it can contribute to the union along with other points.

So to get hypervolume>0, we need at least one point that dominates r=(18,6), i.e., f1<18 and f2<6.
